one_liner: A part-time role at George Mason University helping run hiring searches: posting jobs, screening applicants, scheduling interviews and coordinating with search committees.
fit_summary: Daniel's recruiting work at the National Language Service Corps (screening resumes, matching candidates to requests, scripted interviews) and his help with onboarding and offboarding at IEM fit a recruiting coordinator role well. The posting has no description, and a part-time university HR job is only a small step toward his goal of a government career.
eligibility: Open to the public as a Virginia state (university) position; no federal status, clearance or veterans' preference is indicated, but confirm on the full posting.
No education, license or experience requirements are listed here, so read the full posting on jobs.virginia.gov or GMU's careers site before applying.
The role is part-time and on-site in Fairfax (not remote), so confirm hours, schedule and whether benefits apply.
No closing date is stated (open until filled), so earlier applicants may be reviewed first.
strategy: Pull the full position description (GMU often posts it at jobs.gmu.edu) before writing anything, and use its duty and qualification terms where they are true, because the summary here has no description.

Describe your IEM experience by the coordination tasks you actually did, such as scheduling, stakeholder outreach, managing deadlines or supporting government clients, and use recruiting-adjacent wording like 'coordinated' and 'communicated with stakeholders.'
Lead with your people skills: building relationships, representing an organization to the public, and keeping several parties informed during a process.
Write a brief cover letter explaining why you want this role. Present it as an entry point into Virginia public-sector work and campus engagement, and note that you live nearby in Manassas.
Apply soon since there is no deadline, and check whether the Virginia portal requires you to complete its application fields fully rather than only uploading a resume.
Use Virginia state resume norms rather than the federal two-page format, though a concise one-to-two-page resume still works well.
resume_bullets: Screened resumes, matched registered volunteers to Department of Defense language requests and conducted 10 scripted interviews for the National Language Service Corps (2018).
Helped sequence onboarding for FEMA Public Assistance employees by organizing spreadsheets (2019–2020) and assisted with employee onboarding and offboarding at IEM (2019–2024).
Booked flights for corporate-level staff and answered travel-expense questions in Certify.
interview_questions: How would you manage several faculty or staff searches at once with competing deadlines?
Tell us about a time you kept multiple stakeholders informed and aligned on a process.
How would you handle confidential applicant information and questions from candidates about their status?
What did you do at IEM, and how does it prepare you for coordinating searches?
watch_outs: No salary, hours or job description were provided, so verify pay, schedule and benefits for this part-time role before investing time.
Part-time wage positions often lack full state benefits and may not provide a stable path to a full-time role.
The role is HR-focused rather than policy-focused, so weigh whether it builds toward your public policy goals.
